messages:

Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novapay.com>

Subject: Clarify billing for session reuse / prefix cache hits

Hi Vivek,

Quick question as we're reviewing the pricing draft for the NovaPay pilot: our chat flows reuse session IDs heavily (session affinity on the client) and we often replay identical prompts at the start of a session (greetings + user profile snippet). When the same prefix is already in your prompt cache, do you charge us for the input tokens on subsequent messages, or only for the tokens that the model actually generates?

Two specific scenarios:
- Full cache hit (the cached response is returned without invoking model compute)
- Partial cache hit (prefix present but model generates additional tokens)

Also, would cache-hit behavior differ between hosted API and Dedicated? Any recommended contract language or measurable thresholds we should use to claim credits or discounts if our workload shows high cache-hit rates?

I've attached a very small session excerpt so you can see how our clients reuse session state (session-excerpt.txt).

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
CTO, NovaPay
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify billing for session reuse / prefix cache hits

Hi Samir — thanks for the detail and the excerpt. Looping in Marissa (your account lead) to align commercial language.

Short answer (hosted API):
- If a request is served entirely from our prompt/prefix cache (exact key match), there is no "generation" token charge for the output tokens because the model did not execute.
- Input tokens (the bytes you send as the request prefix) are evaluated for metering differently: for hosted API we meter request input tokens as part of the API call, but when the response is a full cache hit we apply a small per-request lookup fee instead of full generation billing.
- For partial cache hits we charge for the tokens the model actually generates; the cached prefix portion reduces model compute but you will see generation tokens for the new output.

Dedicated: behavior is equivalent functionally, but we can surface different reporting and optionally a custom metering rule in a Dedicated contract (e.g., a fixed discounted lookup fee or a cache-hit credit).

What I want to confirm before we commit language: the exact cache key we use includes model name + pinned version + prefix_hash + session_affinity_id (if you send one). That means if you tiebreak sessions on the client side but change any prefix content (timestamp, dynamic id) the cache won't hit. Our engineering team can run a short analysis on the session-excerpt to estimate realistic hit rate.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa will run a quick modeling exercise to show invoice impact at 50/70/90% hit rates.
- If NovaPay shows sustained >70% full cache hits on a route, we can include a cache-credit clause in the Dedicated contract or a usage credit for hosted customers.

Attaching a short note internally — I'll have Marissa follow up with a spreadsheet and a term draft.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Vivek — quick internal note before we reply with numbers. I modeled a few options in cache-credit-modeling.xlsx (attached):

Option A (hosted, no contract amendment): automatic per-request lookup fee of $0.0005 for full cache hits; generation tokens charged normally when model executes. Simpler operationally, clear on invoices.

Option B (hosted, committed customer): if full cache-hit ratio >= 70% for a billing cycle, we issue a 30% credit on generation-line items for that route and waive lookup fees.

Option C (Dedicated / Enterprise): allow a negotiated fixed-rate lookup (e.g., $0.0002) and explicit credit schedule (70/85/95% thresholds).

My recommended starting point for NovaPay: propose Option B in a one-page amendment. Keeps self-serve metric behavior for the pilot but gives a path to lower unit economics if cache is demonstrably high.

I also drafted a short term (cache-hit-credit-term-draft.pdf). If we agree, we should get legal to rubber-stamp and then present to Samir + procurement.

Marissa

Samir / Elena — following up with a concrete proposal and example invoice lines as you requested. Attached: cache-hit-credit-term-draft.pdf and the modeling workbook.

Technical summary (for your procurement/legal team):
- Full cache hit: output tokens are served from cache; generation tokens = 0 for that call. We will not bill generation token units for cached outputs on hosted API.
- We will still record the call for usage and capacity enforcement; for hosted customers, we charge a nominal lookup fee (proposed default $0.0005 per full cache hit) to cover storage/lookup overhead. That fee can be waived under a committed usage amendment.
- Partial hit: we charge generation tokens for any tokens the model produces beyond the cached prefix.
- Session-affinity: if you include a stable session_affinity_id in the request we will include it in the cache key; this increases chance of hits for multi-turn reuse. If your client emits ephemeral IDs, hits will drop.

Commercial proposal (one-page amendment):
- Pilot period (3 months): standard hosted billing + lookup fee. Redwood will run hit-rate reporting and provide an invoice example.
- If a route shows >=70% full cache hits across the pilot, Redwood issues a 30% credit on generation-line items for that route for the next billing quarter and refunds lookup fees for the pilot period.

Example invoice snippet (for a single chat route):
- Generation tokens: 120,000 tokens — billed at $0.0006/token = $72.00 (after credits that number may be reduced)
- Cache lookup fees: 40,000 full cache hits x $0.0005 = $20.00
- Net (pre-credit): $92.00

If you like, we can convert the one-page amendment into a short SOW and route to procurement. Would you prefer we route the amendment through your HubSpot deal (I can attach to DEAL-8391) or send a lightweight DocuSign?

Next steps:
- Tell us whether you want lookup fees counted in committed baseline or excluded (our recommendation: exclude them from baseline commits; base the commit on generation units).
- If you want, we can run a 48-72 hour extraction against a sample of traffic to estimate expected hit rate before the pilot starts.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
